choices.text: A three-drug regimen begun only after an exposure occurs

choices.label: C
choices.text: An NNRTI/NRTI combination taken before any exposure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Weekly azithromycin to prevent opportunistic infection

explanation.summary: Pre-exposure prophylaxis with an NNRTI/NRTI combination is offered to high-risk populations such as MSM, sex workers, and IV drug users.
explanation.whyCorrect: Certain people, such as intravenous drug users, sex workers, and men who have sex with men, are at higher risk for HIV infection. For these at-risk populations a PrEP NNRTI/NRTI combination can be offered, along with education and encouragement of condom use. Risk should be determined from a detailed sexual and substance use history.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A boosted protease inhibitor is a treatment component, not the combination offered for pre-exposure prophylaxis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A three-drug regimen after exposure is postexposure prophylaxis, which does not address his ongoing risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prevents Pneumocystis and toxoplasmosis in AIDS, not HIV infection itself.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Azithromycin prevents Mycobacterium avium complex in advanced AIDS and does not prevent HIV acquisition.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man with HIV infection has a CD4 cell count of 150/mm3. In addition to antiretroviral therapy, which of the following is most appropriate to prevent Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia?

explanation.summary: TMP-SMX is used to prevent Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia once the CD4 count falls below 200/mm3.
explanation.whyCorrect: Commonly, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is used to prevent P jiroveci pneumonia for a CD4 count below 200/mm3. This patient's count of 150/mm3 is below that threshold. The same drug also covers toxoplasmosis once the count drops below 100/mm3.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin is used for Mycobacterium avium complex once the CD4 count falls below 50/mm3.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Enfuvirtide is a fusion inhibitor used to treat HIV, not to prevent opportunistic infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nevirapine is an NNRTI used against HIV itself and does not prevent Pneumocystis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ritonavir is a pharmacokinetic enhancer and protease inhibitor with no antiparasitic activity.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman with HIV infection is receiving trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Her physician notes that this same drug also provides protection against toxoplasmosis once her CD4 count drops below a particular value. Which of the following is that threshold?

explanation.summary: Toxoplasmosis prophylaxis with TMP-SMX begins when the CD4 count falls below 100/mm3.
explanation.whyCorrect: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is used to prevent P jiroveci pneumonia for a CD4 count below 200/mm3 and toxoplasmosis for counts below 100/mm3. The same agent therefore covers two different opportunistic infections at two different thresholds as immunosuppression deepens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 50/mm3 is the threshold at which Mycobacterium avium complex prophylaxis is considered.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 200/mm3 is the threshold for Pneumocystis prophylaxis, not for toxoplasmosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 350/mm3 is above any of the prophylaxis thresholds described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 500/mm3 is well above the counts at which opportunistic infection prophylaxis is started.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman with AIDS has a CD4 cell count of 30/mm3. She is already taking trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and has just been started on an effective antiretroviral regimen. Regarding azithromycin for Mycobacterium avium complex, which of the following statements is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is contraindicated together with integrase strand transfer inhibitors

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is indicated only once the CD4 count falls below 200/mm3

choices.label: C
choices.text: It must be continued lifelong regardless of antiretroviral therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: It should replace trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole in her regimen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Newer guidance suggests antiretroviral therapy alone is enough

explanation.summary: MAC prophylaxis with azithromycin is considered below a CD4 count of 50/mm3, but newer guidelines suggest antiretroviral therapy alone suffices.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once the CD4 count goes lower than 50/mm3, Mycobacterium avium complex may be prevented with azithromycin. However, newer guidelines suggest that antiretroviral therapy alone is enough, because suppressing viral RNA restores the CD4 count. This patient is below the 50/mm3 threshold but is now on effective therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No interaction between azithromycin and integrase inhibitors is described; the CYP450 interactions discussed involve efavirenz and the boosters.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 200/mm3 is the Pneumocystis threshold; MAC prophylaxis is considered below 50/mm3.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lifelong azithromycin regardless of therapy contradicts the newer guidance that antiretroviral therapy alone is sufficient.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is still needed at her count for Pneumocystis and toxoplasmosis coverage.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man with known HIV infection is admitted with Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia. His CD4 cell count is 140/mm3. Which of the following best describes his condition?

choices.label: E
choices.text: HIV infection with a preserved CD4 count

explanation.summary: AIDS is diagnosed by an AIDS-defining illness such as Pneumocystis pneumonia together with a CD4 count below 200/mm3.
explanation.whyCorrect: AIDS is generally diagnosed with the presence of AIDS-defining illnesses, such as Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia, and a CD4 cell count below 200/mm3. This patient meets both criteria. Starting effective combination therapy can keep the CD4 count up by suppressing viral RNA and reducing the inflammatory immune response.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Abacavir hypersensitivity is a drug reaction linked to HLA-B*5701, not an opportunistic pneumonia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A seroconversion illness is an early event and does not describe a patient with a known diagnosis and an opportunistic infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nothing in the presentation indicates a failing regimen; he has an AIDS-defining illness at a low CD4 count.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A CD4 count of 140/mm3 is not preserved; it is below the threshold that defines AIDS.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 10 weeks' gestation is newly diagnosed with HIV infection and is ready to begin antiretroviral therapy. Which of the following nucleoside/nucleotide backbones is preferred in pregnancy?

explanation.summary: In pregnancy the preferred NRTI backbones are tenofovir DF plus emtricitabine, or abacavir plus lamivudine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Therapy does change in the pregnant patient. For the NRTI component, the drugs of choice are tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and emtricitabine, or abacavir and lamivudine. The third drug is generally a protease inhibitor in the first trimester or an integrase inhibitor afterward, and treatment during pregnancy reduces mother-to-child transmission to less than 2%.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Abacavir is paired with lamivudine, not with zidovudine, in the preferred backbones.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Didanosine is not a preferred agent, so this pairing is not used.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Stavudine is not among the agents named as drugs of choice for the pregnant patient.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Didanosine is rarely used at all because of the risk of pancreatitis and other complications.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 30-year-old pregnant woman with HIV infection is counseled about the benefit of taking antiretroviral therapy throughout her pregnancy. Transmission of HIV to her infant can be reduced to approximately which of the following?

explanation.summary: Antiretroviral therapy during pregnancy lowers mother-to-child transmission to less than 2%.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment during pregnancy can reduce mother-to-child transmission to less than 2%. Safety for the fetus must also be taken into account when choosing the specific agents, which is why protease inhibitors are avoided with preterm birth risk and dolutegravir is often avoided in newly diagnosed pregnant patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 15% is far higher than the figure achieved with antiretroviral therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 20% overstates the residual risk with treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 25% overstates the residual risk achievable with effective therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 8% is still well above the stated figure of less than 2%.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman is newly diagnosed with HIV infection at 7 weeks' gestation. Her physician deliberately chooses an integrase inhibitor other than dolutegravir for her regimen. Which of the following best explains this decision?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Risk of fetal bone marrow suppression

choices.label: D
choices.text: Risk of neural tube defects in the fetus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Risk of preterm birth with this agent

explanation.summary: Dolutegravir is sometimes avoided in newly diagnosed pregnant patients because of the risk for neural tube defects.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dolutegravir may be continued in pregnant patients who are already taking it, but it is sometimes avoided in newly diagnosed patients because of the risk for neural tube defects. This patient is newly diagnosed and in the first trimester, the window in which the neural tube closes, so an alternative is selected.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone marrow suppression with neutropenia is an adverse effect of zidovudine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The distinctive hypersensitivity reaction belongs to abacavir and is linked to HLA-B*5701.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pancreatitis is a complication of the NRTI didanosine and of NRTI mitochondrial toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Preterm birth risk is the reason protease inhibitors are generally avoided in at-risk pregnancies, not dolutegravir.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 30-year-old pregnant woman with HIV infection has a history of preterm delivery and a shortened cervix on ultrasonography. Which of the following antiretroviral classes is generally avoided in this situation?

explanation.summary: Protease inhibitors are generally avoided in pregnant patients at risk for preterm birth.
explanation.whyCorrect: Safety for the fetus must be considered when choosing the third drug in pregnancy. Although a protease inhibitor is generally the third drug in the first trimester, for pregnant patients at risk for preterm birth protease inhibitors are generally avoided. An integrase inhibitor would be the usual alternative, with the dolutegravir caveat in newly diagnosed patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CCR5 antagonists are not discussed as a pregnancy concern; maraviroc is reserved for drug-resistant virus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Integrase inhibitors are the alternative third drug in pregnancy, with only dolutegravir carrying a specific caution.
whyWrongByChoice.C: NNRTIs are not the class singled out for avoidance because of preterm birth risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: NRTIs form the preferred backbone in pregnancy and are not avoided for preterm birth risk.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man is newly diagnosed with HIV infection. Before therapy is chosen, his physician orders a genetic test that is required in every HIV-positive patient, whether or not the relevant drug will be used. Which of the following is that test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone mineral density by DEXA scanning

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum tenofovir concentration at steady state

explanation.summary: All HIV-positive patients must be tested for HLA-B*5701 because of the abacavir hypersensitivity reaction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Abacavir has a unique hypersensitivity reaction. All patients who are HIV positive must have genetic testing to determine whether the HLA-B*5701 allele is present, regardless of whether abacavir will be part of their medication regimen. This is a pharmacogenomic requirement, not a drug level or organ function test.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone density testing is not the universal requirement, although tenofovir DF can cause bone loss.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CYP2C19 genotyping is not required; the CYP450 issues here concern induction and inhibition by drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: G6PD activity is not the genetic test required for all HIV-positive patients in this brick.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tenofovir levels are not routinely measured; toxicity is managed by choosing TAF over TDF.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 46-year-old man with HIV infection develops neutropenia several months after starting therapy. A bone marrow examination shows suppression of all lineages. Which of the following agents in his regimen is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Zidovudine characteristically causes bone marrow suppression with neutropenia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the NRTIs, each has a characteristic toxicity on top of the shared mitochondrial toxicity. Zidovudine, a thymidine analogue, may cause bone marrow suppression with neutropenia. Recognizing the drug-specific toxicities allows the offending agent to be swapped rather than abandoning the class.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Didanosine characteristically causes pancreatitis, which is why it is rarely used.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Efavirenz is an NNRTI associated with CNS toxicity, QT prolongation, and raised hepatic enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Raltegravir is an integrase inhibitor, a class that usually causes few adverse effects.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tenofovir characteristically causes kidney injury or bone loss, particularly in the disoproxil fumarate form.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A pharmacist reviewing an older HIV formulary notes that one nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor is now rarely prescribed because of the risk of pancreatitis and other complications. Which of the following is that drug?

explanation.summary: Didanosine is rarely used today because of its risk of pancreatitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Didanosine may cause pancreatitis, and in fact it is rarely used because of the risk of complications. Pancreatitis and neuropathy are the general manifestations of NRTI mitochondrial toxicity, but didanosine carries enough of this risk to have fallen out of routine use.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Abacavir is limited by hypersensitivity tied to HLA-B*5701, not by pancreatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Emtricitabine is a cytosine analogue widely used in first-line and pre-exposure regimens.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lamivudine is a cytosine analogue that remains in common use, including in pregnancy with abacavir.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tenofovir is one of the most common HIV medications; its issues are renal injury and bone loss.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man has been taking a tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-containing regimen for several years. His serum creatinine has risen and bone densitometry shows new osteopenia. His viral load is undetectable and he wishes to stay on a tenofovir-based regimen. Which of the following is the most appropriate change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add azithromycin to slow further loss of bone density

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add ritonavir to boost the tenofovir concentration further

choices.label: C
choices.text: Replace tenofovir with didanosine within the same regimen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Switch to tenofovir alafenamide in place of the current form

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switch to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate from the current form

explanation.summary: Tenofovir alafenamide has a much lower rate of renal injury and bone loss than tenofovir disoproxil fumarate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tenofovir exists as two prodrugs, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and tenofovir alafenamide, which work the same mechanistically. TDF produces much higher plasma levels and is much more likely to cause renal injury and bone loss, while TAF has a significantly lower rate of these adverse effects and is the preferred form. Nowadays, when clinicians refer to tenofovir, TAF is implied.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin is used for Mycobacterium avium complex prophylaxis and has no effect on bone density.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Boosting would raise tenofovir exposure and worsen the very toxicities that prompted the change.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Didanosine is rarely used because of the risk of pancreatitis and would be a poor substitution.
whyWrongByChoice.E: He is already taking the disoproxil fumarate form, which is the one causing his renal and bone toxicity.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man taking a nucleoside analogue-containing regimen for HIV infection develops a painful peripheral neuropathy and an episode of pancreatitis. Which of the following best explains this pattern of toxicity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blockade of the CCR5 coreceptor on peripheral neural tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immune complex deposition triggered by the HLA-B*5701 allele

choices.label: C
choices.text: Induction of hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes by the analogue

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of human DNA polymerases, with mitochondrial injury

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibition of viral protease within host mitochondria

explanation.summary: NRTIs inhibit human DNA polymerases in addition to reverse transcriptase, producing mitochondrial toxicity.
explanation.whyCorrect: The important adverse effects of NRTIs have to do with mitochondrial toxicity, because these drugs inhibit human DNA polymerases as well as HIV's reverse transcriptase. This can present as pancreatitis or neuropathy. Individual agents add their own toxicities on top of this class effect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CCR5 blockade is the mechanism of maraviroc, an entry inhibitor, and is unrelated to this toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HLA-B*5701 underlies the abacavir hypersensitivity reaction, not pancreatitis with neuropathy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Efavirenz, an NNRTI, is the CYP450 inducer discussed, and induction does not cause neuropathy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nucleoside analogues do not act on protease; protease inhibitors cause metabolic effects instead.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man with HIV infection is started on efavirenz. Which of the following adverse effects should be specifically monitored for in this patient?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nephrotoxicity and loss of bone mineral

explanation.summary: Efavirenz requires monitoring for CNS toxicity, QT prolongation, and elevated hepatic enzymes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The NNRTI efavirenz must be monitored because of central nervous system toxicity and QT prolongation, in addition to increases in hepatic enzymes. Within the same class, rilpivirine instead causes depression and insomnia, so the NNRTIs are not interchangeable in their toxicity profiles.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone marrow suppression with neutropenia is the signature toxicity of zidovudine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Insulin resistance and hyperlipidemia are protease inhibitor class effects.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Renal injury and bone loss are characteristic of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pancreatitis and neuropathy reflect NRTI mitochondrial toxicity, not an NNRTI effect.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman taking a regimen that includes the non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor rilpivirine reports several weeks of low mood and difficulty falling asleep. Which of the following adverse effects is characteristic of this particular agent?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nephrotoxicity with loss of bone mineral

choices.label: E
choices.text: Severe rash with fever and raised liver enzymes

explanation.summary: Rilpivirine may cause depression and insomnia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the NNRTIs, efavirenz is monitored for CNS toxicity and QT prolongation, whereas rilpivirine may cause depression and insomnia. Her symptoms match the described toxicity of the specific agent she is taking rather than a class-wide effect.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hyperlipidemia and diabetes are general protease inhibitor effects, not NNRTI effects.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Renal injury and bone loss point to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pancreatitis and neuropathy reflect the mitochondrial toxicity of the nucleoside analogues.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Severe rash with fever and elevated liver enzymes is characteristic of the protease inhibitor darunavir.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man with HIV infection develops a severe diffuse rash with fever three weeks after a boosted protease inhibitor was added to his regimen. Serum aminotransferase levels are elevated. Which of the following agents is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Darunavir is the protease inhibitor associated with severe rash, fever, and elevated liver enzymes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Protease inhibitors as a class may cause diabetes or insulin resistance, hyperlipidemia, and dyslipidemia. Specifically, darunavir may cause severe rash and fever with elevated liver enzymes. Boosting with ritonavir may limit these adverse effects by allowing lower doses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Atazanavir has been known to be nephrotoxic rather than to cause severe rash with fever.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cobicistat is a booster that inhibits CYP450 and has no intrinsic antiviral activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lopinavir is a commonly boosted protease inhibitor but is not linked to this specific rash and fever.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ritonavir is used here as the pharmacokinetic booster and is not the agent linked to this reaction.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 42-year-old man has been virologically suppressed on a bictegravir-containing regimen. After efavirenz is substituted for another component, his bictegravir concentrations fall to subtherapeutic levels. Which of the following best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bictegravir induces its own metabolism when it is boosted

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bictegravir is eliminated unchanged by the kidney

choices.label: C
choices.text: Efavirenz displaces bictegravir from its plasma protein sites

choices.label: D
choices.text: Efavirenz induces CYP450, which clears bictegravir

choices.label: E
choices.text: Efavirenz inhibits CYP450, which slows bictegravir clearance

explanation.summary: Efavirenz induces CYP450 and lowers levels of drugs cleared by that system, such as bictegravir.
explanation.whyCorrect: An important concept in antiretroviral therapy is CYP450 induction or inhibition. Efavirenz is an NNRTI that induces CYP450 and may decrease levels of certain drugs, such as bictegravir, an integrase inhibitor cleared by CYP450. Combining antiretrovirals that induce or inhibit CYP450 can change the levels of other drugs used in the combination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoinduction by bictegravir is not described; the change followed the addition of efavirenz.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bictegravir is specifically noted to be cleared by CYP450, which is why the interaction occurs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Protein binding displacement is not the interaction mechanism described for antiretrovirals here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Efavirenz induces rather than inhibits CYP450; inhibition is the action of ritonavir and cobicistat.

questions.topicName: Antiretrovirals: Drugs to Treat and Prevent HIV Infection

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman develops fever, myalgia, and cough during influenza season. A rapid influenza test is positive, and she is started on oseltamivir. Which of the following is the mechanism of action of this drug?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blockade of the M2 ion channel

explanation.summary: Oseltamivir and zanamivir treat influenza by inhibiting the viral enzyme neuraminidase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Neuraminidase inhibitors are the mainstay of influenza treatment, and oseltamivir is the current drug of choice. Neuraminidase is a viral enzyme that releases budding viruses from the infected cell's outer membrane, so blocking it reduces the rate at which newly formed virions reach healthy cells and slows the progression of infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neuraminidase inhibitors act at viral release, not at the receptor-binding step of entry.
whyWrongByChoice.B: M2 ion channel blockade is the mechanism of amantadine and rimantadine, not oseltamivir.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibition of viral DNA polymerase describes guanosine analogs such as acyclovir and ganciclovir.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Activity against viral RNA polymerase describes ribavirin, the agent used for RSV.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 41-year-old man with influenza is treated with zanamivir. Which step of the viral life cycle is most directly interrupted by this drug?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attachment to the host cell receptor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endocytosis of the virion into the cell

choices.label: D
choices.text: Release of progeny virions from the cell

explanation.summary: Neuraminidase inhibitors act at the release-of-progeny-virus step of the influenza life cycle.
explanation.whyCorrect: Neuraminidase frees budding virions from the outer membrane of the infected cell. Oseltamivir and zanamivir block that enzyme, so newly formed virus stays tethered to the cell it came from and fewer particles travel on to healthy cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Virion assembly proceeds normally; only the final release of the particles is blocked.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Receptor binding occurs before the drug's target step and is unaffected by neuraminidase inhibition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endocytosis brings the virion into the cell and is not the step these drugs block.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Genome replication is the target of nucleic acid synthesis inhibitors such as ribavirin.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with laboratory-confirmed influenza and asthma is seen 1 day after symptom onset. Which of the following is the current drug of choice for treating his influenza?

explanation.summary: Oseltamivir is the current drug of choice for influenza.
explanation.whyCorrect: Neuraminidase inhibitors are the mainstay of influenza management, and among them oseltamivir is the current drug of choice. Comorbid asthma also places this patient at increased risk of progressing to severe influenza, which supports treating him.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acyclovir is a guanosine analog used for HSV and VZV infections.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Amantadine is an M2 ion channel blocker formerly used for influenza but discontinued because of resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ganciclovir is a guanosine analog used for cytomegalovirus infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ribavirin is the drug used for RSV and hepatitis C, not for influenza.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman asks when influenza antiviral therapy must be started to be effective. Which of the following describes the window of maximum effectiveness?

choices.label: B
choices.text: At any point during the illness

explanation.summary: Influenza antivirals have maximum effectiveness when started within 48 hours of symptom onset.
explanation.whyCorrect: These drugs work best when given in the first 48 hours after symptoms begin. After that window, the drug does not provide any additional benefit, so the timing of the first dose is the single most important determinant of whether therapy helps.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Waiting for defervescence would push treatment past the window of benefit.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Timing is crucial; the drugs are not equally useful at any point in the illness.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Waiting for hypoxemia would delay therapy well beyond the effective window.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Seven days is far outside the effective window; benefit is lost after 48 hours.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man with influenza presents 4 days after symptom onset and asks why oseltamivir is unlikely to help him now. Which of the following best explains the loss of benefit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Neutralizing antibody binds the drug and inactivates it after several days

choices.label: B
choices.text: Resistance mutations arise in nearly every strain by the fourth day

choices.label: C
choices.text: The drug is cleared too rapidly to reach the airway this late in illness

choices.label: D
choices.text: The virus switches to cell-to-cell spread that the drug cannot block

choices.label: E
choices.text: Viral budding has slowed, so there is little neuraminidase activity left to block

explanation.summary: After 48 hours the rate of new virion budding is very low, so a neuraminidase inhibitor has little left to do.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oseltamivir works by keeping budding virions tethered to the infected cell's outer membrane. Past the 48-hour mark the rate of newly formed virus is very low, so blocking neuraminidase is essentially ineffective because the virus is no longer budding.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibody does not inactivate oseltamivir, and this is not the reason for the 48-hour rule.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Resistance from mutations occurs in some strains, but most circulating strains remain susceptible.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Drug clearance does not change with the day of illness; the problem is the absence of the target activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The explanation for late failure is reduced budding, not a switch in the mode of viral spread.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman with influenza is prescribed an antiviral given as an inhaled aerosol powder. Which of the following adverse effects is most likely?

explanation.summary: Zanamivir is inhaled, and its adverse effects reflect that route: airway and nasal irritation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Neuraminidase inhibitors are generally well tolerated, and their side effects track with the route of administration. Zanamivir is an inhaled aerosol powder and primarily causes airway irritation, along with headache, sore throat, and myalgia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acute kidney injury is not a reported adverse effect of zanamivir.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemolytic anemia is the black box adverse effect of ribavirin, not of an inhaled neuraminidase inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peripheral neuropathy is not among the reported adverse effects of these drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Photosensitivity is not an adverse effect associated with neuraminidase inhibitors.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man takes an oral neuraminidase inhibitor for influenza and calls about a side effect. Which of the following is he most likely to report?

explanation.summary: Oseltamivir is given orally and mainly causes headache and gastrointestinal upset.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adverse effects of neuraminidase inhibitors follow their route of administration. Because oseltamivir is swallowed, it mainly produces gastrointestinal disturbance such as nausea and vomiting, along with headache.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Airway irritation is characteristic of inhaled zanamivir rather than oral oseltamivir.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hearing loss is not an adverse effect associated with these antiviral agents.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hemolytic anemia is an adverse effect of ribavirin, which is used for RSV and hepatitis C.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neutropenia is reported with ribavirin therapy, not with oral neuraminidase inhibitors.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 58-year-old lung transplant recipient with severe RSV infection is given ribavirin. Which of the following best describes how this drug works?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blocks the M2 ion channel and prevents viral uncoating

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blocks viral attachment to host sialic acid receptors

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibits guanine nucleotide synthesis and halts strand elongation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibits viral neuraminidase and blocks virion release

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibits viral protease and prevents polyprotein cleavage

explanation.summary: Ribavirin is a guanine nucleotide synthesis inhibitor that mimics purine structure and stops viral nucleic acid elongation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ribavirin is a broad-spectrum nucleoside antiviral that mimics purine structure. It competitively inhibits nucleic acid synthesis by being incorporated into the growing nucleic acid strand and halting elongation, which decreases viral replication.

whyWrongByChoice.A: M2 channel blockade describes amantadine and rimantadine, which are no longer used for influenza.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ribavirin acts inside the cell on nucleic acid synthesis, not at the attachment step.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neuraminidase inhibition describes oseltamivir and zanamivir, which are used for influenza.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Protease inhibition is not the mechanism of ribavirin as described for RSV therapy.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: Five patients with respiratory syncytial virus infection are evaluated. Which of the following patients is the most appropriate candidate for antiviral therapy with ribavirin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 30-year-old with a mild RSV upper respiratory infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 70-year-old with treated hypertension and an RSV cough

choices.label: C
choices.text: A bone marrow transplant recipient with severe RSV pneumonia

choices.label: D
choices.text: A healthy 2-year-old with RSV bronchiolitis and a good appetite

choices.label: E
choices.text: A woman in the third trimester of pregnancy with RSV

explanation.summary: Ribavirin for RSV is reserved for severely immunocompromised patients, such as transplant recipients.
explanation.whyCorrect: RSV is usually self-limiting and managed supportively. Antiviral therapy with ribavirin is only indicated in patients who are severely immunocompromised, such as transplant patients or those with certain cancers, and even then it must be considered carefully and individualized because of the drug's risks.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mild RSV upper respiratory illness is self-limiting and requires no antiviral therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Well-controlled hypertension does not make a patient severely immunocompromised.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A healthy toddler with bronchiolitis is managed with supportive care, not ribavirin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ribavirin is an FDA category X drug and is contraindicated in pregnancy.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A previously healthy 9-month-old infant has rhinorrhea, cough, and low-grade fever from RSV. He is feeding well and has normal oxygen saturation. Which of the following is the preferred management?

explanation.summary: The preferred treatment of RSV infection is no antiviral treatment, because the infection is self-limiting.
explanation.whyCorrect: RSV is a self-limiting infection, so the preferred approach is supportive care: maintaining oxygenation, replenishing fluids, and managing symptoms. Antiviral therapy is reserved for severely immunocompromised patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acyclovir is a guanosine analog used for HSV and VZV infections.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Oseltamivir treats influenza and has no activity against RSV.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ribavirin is restricted to severely immunocompromised patients because of its risks.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Zanamivir is a neuraminidase inhibitor for influenza, not an RSV drug.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 3-year-old with known asthma has an RSV lower respiratory tract infection with cough and diffuse wheezing. Which of the following is most likely to relieve his symptoms?

explanation.summary: In RSV lower respiratory tract infection with cough and wheezing, bronchodilators and steroids may relieve symptoms, especially with underlying reactive airway disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Management of RSV is supportive. In patients with lower respiratory tract infection who present with cough and wheezing, bronchodilators and steroids may result in symptom relief, particularly when the patient has underlying reactive airway disease such as asthma or COPD.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ribavirin is reserved for severely immunocompromised patients with RSV.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antibiotics do not treat a viral lower respiratory tract infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Amantadine was an influenza drug and is no longer used because of resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oseltamivir is an influenza drug and has no role in RSV infection.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman is counseled before starting ribavirin. Which of the following adverse effects carries an FDA black box warning for this drug?

explanation.summary: Hemolytic anemia is the black box warning issued by the FDA for ribavirin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ribavirin is associated with anemia, hemolytic anemia, and neutropenia. The hemolytic anemia is serious enough that it carries an FDA black box warning, because the resulting anemia can worsen preexisting cardiac disease.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hepatic failure is not the black box warning attached to ribavirin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nephrotoxicity is not the warned-about toxicity for this drug.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stevens-Johnson syndrome is not a described ribavirin adverse effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Torsades de pointes is not among ribavirin's reported adverse effects.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman who is 14 weeks pregnant is hospitalized with a severe respiratory viral infection. Which of the following drugs is contraindicated because it is a proven teratogen?

explanation.summary: Ribavirin is an FDA category X drug and is contraindicated in pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The FDA has classified ribavirin as a category X drug, meaning it is contraindicated in pregnant patients. It is a proven teratogen, a substance that causes birth defects when a pregnant mother is exposed to it, and any benefit it provides is outweighed by that risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amantadine is an M2 channel blocker that was abandoned for resistance, not teratogenicity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Oseltamivir is not classified as a category X teratogen in this brick's discussion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rimantadine, like amantadine, was discontinued because of viral resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Zanamivir is an inhaled neuraminidase inhibitor and is not the category X drug.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation requires a course of ribavirin. Which of the following is most likely to occur during treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both drugs must be stopped because the pair is contraindicated

choices.label: B
choices.text: His anticoagulant effect will fall and require higher warfarin doses

choices.label: C
choices.text: His INR will rise sharply and require vitamin K reversal

choices.label: D
choices.text: No interaction is expected, since neither drug affects the other

choices.label: E
choices.text: Warfarin will raise ribavirin levels and require a dose cut

explanation.summary: Ribavirin diminishes the anticoagulant effect of vitamin K antagonists such as warfarin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ribavirin may diminish the anticoagulant effect of vitamin K antagonists. A patient who needs ribavirin while taking warfarin will require increased warfarin doses or alternate anticoagulation while completing the antiviral course.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The combination is managed with dose adjustment or alternate anticoagulation, not prohibited.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The interaction reduces rather than potentiates anticoagulation, so a sharp INR rise is not expected.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An interaction does exist, which is why anticoagulation must be adjusted.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The described interaction runs from ribavirin to warfarin, not the reverse.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man is starting an antiviral agent for influenza. Administration of live influenza virus vaccine should be avoided during which of the following intervals?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At no time, because no interaction exists between them

choices.label: B
choices.text: Within 2 weeks before or 48 hours after the antiviral

choices.label: C
choices.text: Within 24 hours before or 24 hours after the antiviral

choices.label: D
choices.text: Within 48 hours before or 2 weeks after the antiviral

choices.label: E
choices.text: Within 6 weeks before or 6 weeks after the antiviral

explanation.summary: Live influenza virus vaccine should not be given within 2 weeks before or 48 hours after antiviral agents.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antiviral agents may diminish the therapeutic effect of the influenza virus vaccine. For that reason, administration of live influenza virus vaccine is avoided within 2 weeks before or 48 hours after administration of antiviral agents.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An interaction does exist, because antivirals can blunt the vaccine's effect.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A 24-hour buffer on each side is shorter than the recommended intervals.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This reverses the two intervals; the 2-week restriction applies before the antiviral.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Six weeks on either side is far longer than the recommended avoidance intervals.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: An influenza isolate from a patient who failed oseltamivir carries a single amino acid substitution at position 275 of the neuraminidase gene. Which of the following substitutions is present?

explanation.summary: The H275Y mutation swaps histidine for tyrosine at position 275 of neuraminidase and confers oseltamivir resistance.
explanation.whyCorrect: H275Y is a well-known influenza mutation. This genetic change in the neuraminidase gene at amino acid 275 changes a histidine (H) to a tyrosine (Y), and that substitution confers resistance to oseltamivir.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The wild-type residue at position 275 is histidine, not arginine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Asparagine is not the residue that replaces histidine in the H275Y mutation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serine is not involved in the described position 275 substitution.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This reverses the substitution; the wild-type residue at 275 is histidine.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: Surveillance shows reduced susceptibility of some circulating influenza strains to oseltamivir and zanamivir. Which of the following best explains this reduced susceptibility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cleavage of the drug by a viral esterase enzyme

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complete loss of the M2 ion channel target protein

choices.label: C
choices.text: Efflux pumps that remove the drug from infected cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mutations in neuraminidase that reduce enzyme inhibition

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thickening of the viral envelope that limits drug entry

explanation.summary: Influenza resistance to neuraminidase inhibitors comes mainly from mutations in the neuraminidase itself.
explanation.whyCorrect: Influenza strains can demonstrate resistance through various mutations, with or without exposure to medication. Reduced susceptibility of circulating viruses to neuraminidase inhibitors is mainly due to mutations in the neuraminidase that directly reduce inhibition of enzyme activity. Despite this, the majority of strains remain susceptible.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enzymatic destruction of the drug is not how influenza resists neuraminidase inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The M2 channel is the target of amantadine, not of neuraminidase inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Efflux pumps are a bacterial resistance strategy and are not the mechanism described for influenza.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Envelope thickening is not a described mechanism of influenza antiviral resistance.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A student asks why amantadine and rimantadine, which block the influenza M2 ion channel, are no longer used to treat influenza. Which of the following is the reason?

explanation.summary: The M2 ion channel blockers were discontinued for influenza because of high rates of viral resistance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Amantadine and rimantadine are M2 ion channel blockers that were formerly used to treat influenza. They have been discontinued because of high rates of viral resistance, leaving the neuraminidase inhibitors as the mainstay of treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Zanamivir is the inhaled agent; route of administration did not retire these drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cost is not the stated reason these agents fell out of use.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ribavirin is the proven teratogen; teratogenicity is not why these drugs were dropped.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hemolytic anemia is the black box toxicity of ribavirin, not of the M2 blockers.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A hepatology clinic uses ribavirin combined with interferon alfa. Besides respiratory syncytial virus infection, ribavirin is used to treat which of the following?

explanation.summary: Ribavirin is a broad-spectrum nucleoside antiviral used for RSV and hepatitis C.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ribavirin is a broad-spectrum nucleoside antiviral used for many viral infections besides RSV, including hepatitis C, where it is given with interferon alfa. Its guanine analog activity against viral RNA polymerase explains its usefulness against RNA viruses like RSV and hepatitis C virus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cytomegalovirus is treated with the guanosine analog ganciclovir.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Epstein-Barr virus is not listed among the infections ribavirin is used to treat.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Herpes zoster is caused by VZV and is treated with acyclovir and related agents.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Influenza is treated with neuraminidase inhibitors, not ribavirin.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: Five outpatients test positive for influenza. Which of the following patients has a recognized risk factor for progression to severe influenza?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 22-year-old woman with iron deficiency anemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 28-year-old woman who gave birth 10 days ago

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 30-year-old man with seasonal allergic rhinitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: A 35-year-old man with episodic migraine headaches

explanation.summary: Pregnancy or recent delivery within 2 weeks postpartum is a risk factor for severe influenza.
explanation.whyCorrect: Risk factors for progressing to severe influenza include comorbid diabetes, asthma, or chronic kidney or liver disease; age of 65 or more years; pregnancy or recent delivery within 2 weeks postpartum; and immunosuppression. A woman who delivered 10 days ago falls within that postpartum window.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Iron deficiency anemia is not one of the recognized risk conditions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Allergic rhinitis is not among the listed risk factors for severe influenza.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Migraine headache is not a risk factor for progression to severe influenza.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Treated hypothyroidism is not on the list of conditions that increase risk.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: Age alone is enough to place a patient with influenza at increased risk for complications beginning at which of the following ages?

explanation.summary: Age of 65 years or more is a listed risk factor for progression to severe influenza.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the risk factors for progressing to severe influenza is an age of 65 or more years. Patients at or beyond that age are candidates for antiviral treatment even without another comorbid condition.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Forty years is below the threshold at which age alone confers increased risk.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fifty years is below the stated age cutoff.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fifty-five years is still below the stated age cutoff.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Seventy-five is above the threshold but is not where increased risk begins.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with no chronic illnesses is admitted with influenza pneumonia and hypoxemia 1 day after symptom onset. Which of the following best describes the indication for antiviral therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antivirals are indicated only for patients 65 years of age or older

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antivirals are indicated only when a comorbid condition is present

choices.label: C
choices.text: Antivirals are reserved for outpatients with uncomplicated influenza

choices.label: D
choices.text: Antivirals are withheld until supportive care has clearly failed

choices.label: E
choices.text: Severe influenza requiring hospitalization is itself an indication

explanation.summary: Severe influenza requiring hospitalization is an independent indication for antiviral therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Current guidelines recommend antiviral medication for those with severe influenza requiring hospitalization, or for those with influenza plus another condition that increases the risk for complications. Severity alone qualifies this patient, and he is also within the 48-hour window.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Age of 65 or more is a risk factor, not a requirement for treating severe influenza.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A comorbid condition is one indication, but severe illness requiring hospitalization is another.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antivirals may be given to outpatients at clinician discretion, but severe illness is a firm indication.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Supportive care is the foundation of care but antivirals are added, not held in reserve.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A resident asks why antiviral drugs are used at all for influenza and RSV when both infections are self-limiting. Which of the following is the goal of therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To eradicate the virus from the respiratory tract

choices.label: B
choices.text: To minimize symptoms, infectivity, and illness duration

choices.label: C
choices.text: To prevent every case of secondary bacterial pneumonia

choices.label: D
choices.text: To provide lasting immunity against future infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: To remove the need for any supportive care measures

explanation.summary: Because influenza and RSV are self-limiting, the goal of antivirals is to reduce symptoms, infectivity, and duration of illness.
explanation.whyCorrect: Supportive care is the foundation of treating these infections, and antiviral agents are added on top of it. Since both infections are self-limiting, the aim of the antiviral is to minimize symptoms, infectivity, and the duration of illness rather than to cure the infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antivirals slow viral spread rather than eradicating virus from the airway.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Preventing all secondary bacterial pneumonia is not the stated goal of these drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immunity comes from vaccination and infection, not from antiviral therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Supportive care remains the foundation of management even when antivirals are used.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man is admitted with influenza. Before antiviral agents are added, which of the following supportive measures is the foundation of his care?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Strict fluid restriction and aggressive diuresis

explanation.summary: Supportive care for influenza and RSV means maintaining hydration, oxygenation, and a controlled temperature.
explanation.whyCorrect: Supportive care is the foundation of treating influenza and RSV because keeping the patient stable is the priority. The provider must ensure the patient maintains hydration, oxygenation, and a controlled temperature; only once these are addressed are antiviral agents added.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibiotics do not treat a viral infection and are not the foundation of care.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Plasmapheresis has no role in the supportive care of influenza or RSV.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fluid restriction is the opposite of the recommended emphasis on hydration.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immunoglobulin is not part of routine supportive management of these infections.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A public health nurse is describing who suffers the most severe respiratory syncytial virus disease. Which of the following groups is most affected?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Men between 20 and 40 years of age

choices.label: C
choices.text: Newborns and adults older than 60 years

choices.label: D
choices.text: Otherwise healthy adults in their fifties

explanation.summary: RSV is most severe at the extremes of age: the very young and adults over 60.
explanation.whyCorrect: RSV is most severe in the very young, such as newborns, and in elderly populations, meaning those older than 60 years. In most other patients RSV is self-limiting and does not require medication beyond supportive care.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adolescents are not identified as a group at high risk for severe RSV.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Young and middle-aged men are not a recognized high-risk RSV group.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Healthy adults in their fifties fall below the elderly threshold described for severe disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: School-aged children and young adults generally have self-limiting RSV illness.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 66-year-old renal transplant recipient with stable coronary artery disease develops severe RSV pneumonia, and ribavirin is being considered. Which of the following adverse effects most directly raises his risk of myocardial infarction?

explanation.summary: Ribavirin-induced hemolytic anemia can exacerbate preexisting cardiac disease and trigger myocardial infarction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ribavirin causes anemia, hemolytic anemia, and neutropenia. It is believed that the anemia resulting from hemolysis can exacerbate preexisting cardiac disease and trigger myocardial infarction, which is why ribavirin must be used with caution in patients with heart disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Headache and myalgia are reported with therapy but do not threaten the coronary circulation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nasal irritation is an effect of inhaled zanamivir, not of ribavirin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gastrointestinal upset is typical of oral oseltamivir and is not the cardiac concern here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neutropenia raises infection risk rather than precipitating myocardial infarction.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man with no medical history telephones during influenza season with fever, chills, myalgia, and cough that began about 30 hours ago. He takes no medications and asks whether an antiviral would help. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antivirals are contraindicated because he has no comorbid illness

choices.label: B
choices.text: He should be told that antivirals shorten the illness by a week

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oseltamivir may be prescribed because he is within the 48-hour window

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ribavirin should be prescribed because it covers RNA viruses

choices.label: E
choices.text: Therapy should be deferred until symptoms have lasted 72 hours

explanation.summary: Antivirals can be offered to relatively healthy patients at the clinician's discretion when they are still within the 48-hour window.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antiviral medication can be given to relatively healthy patients at the discretion of the clinician, and these drugs have maximum effectiveness when started within 48 hours of symptom onset. At roughly 30 hours he is still inside that window, so oseltamivir is a reasonable option after discussing its modest benefit.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lack of comorbidity does not forbid treatment; it is a matter of clinician discretion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The realistic benefit is feeling better about a day sooner, not a week.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ribavirin is used for RSV and hepatitis C, not for influenza.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Waiting until 72 hours would push him past the window where the drug helps.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A healthy 30-year-old woman has had fever, myalgia, and cough for 4 days. Influenza testing is positive. She is not hypoxic and has no chronic conditions. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aerosolized ribavirin for the duration of illness

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inhaled zanamivir started today for 5 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: Live attenuated influenza vaccine administered today

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral oseltamivir started today for 5 days

choices.label: E
choices.text: Symptomatic supportive care without antiviral therapy

explanation.summary: Past the 48-hour window, influenza antivirals provide no additional benefit, so care is supportive.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antivirals have maximum effectiveness when started within 48 hours of symptom onset, and after that window the drug does not provide any additional benefit. At day 4 in a healthy outpatient, supportive care with hydration and symptom control is appropriate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ribavirin treats RSV in the severely immunocompromised and has no role in influenza.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Zanamivir has the same 48-hour limitation as other neuraminidase inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Live influenza vaccine is avoided around antiviral use and does not treat active illness.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oseltamivir started on day 4 is outside the window in which it adds benefit.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: Neuraminidase is the target of oseltamivir and zanamivir. Which of the following is the normal function of this viral enzyme?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It cleaves the host receptor so the virus can enter

choices.label: B
choices.text: It cleaves viral polyproteins during virion assembly

choices.label: C
choices.text: It copies the viral genome during replication

choices.label: D
choices.text: It pumps protons into the virion during uncoating

choices.label: E
choices.text: It releases budding virions from the cell membrane

explanation.summary: Neuraminidase frees newly budded influenza virions from the infected cell's outer membrane.
explanation.whyCorrect: Neuraminidase is a viral enzyme that releases the budding viruses from an infected cell's outer membrane. Oseltamivir and zanamivir block it, which reduces the rate of newly formed viruses traveling to healthy cells and slows the overall progression of infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neuraminidase acts at release from the cell, not at entry into it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Polyprotein cleavage is a protease function, not a neuraminidase function.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Genome copying is performed by viral polymerase, the target of ribavirin's activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Proton transport during uncoating is the role of the M2 ion channel.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: Oseltamivir and zanamivir are prescribed during respiratory virus season. These drugs are active against which of the following?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Influenza A but not influenza B

choices.label: D
choices.text: RSV and influenza A but not B

explanation.summary: The neuraminidase inhibitors oseltamivir and zanamivir cover influenza A and B.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oseltamivir and zanamivir are neuraminidase inhibitors indicated for influenza A and B. They have no activity against RSV, for which ribavirin is the only drug used.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hepatitis C and RSV are the domain of ribavirin, not of neuraminidase inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coverage is not restricted to influenza A; influenza B is also treated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neuraminidase inhibitors do not treat RSV infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: RSV is treated with ribavirin in select patients, not with neuraminidase inhibitors.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man has recurrent painful vesicles on the vermilion border of his lip. Among the drugs that inhibit viral nucleic acid synthesis, which agent is used for herpes simplex and varicella zoster infections?

explanation.summary: Among nucleic acid synthesis inhibitors, acyclovir is the guanosine analog used for HSV and VZV.
explanation.whyCorrect: The nucleic acid synthesis inhibitors divide into guanosine analogs and guanine nucleotide synthesis inhibitors. Acyclovir and related guanosine analogs are used for HSV and VZV, ganciclovir is used for CMV, and ribavirin, which blocks guanine nucleotide synthesis, is used for RSV and hepatitis C.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ganciclovir is the guanosine analog used for cytomegalovirus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oseltamivir is a neuraminidase inhibitor for influenza and does not affect herpesviruses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ribavirin targets RNA viruses such as RSV and hepatitis C virus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Zanamivir is an inhaled neuraminidase inhibitor used only for influenza.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: Ribavirin is effective against a range of RNA viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus and hepatitis C virus. Its activity as a guanine analog is directed against which of the following viral targets?

explanation.summary: As a guanine analog, ribavirin acts against viral RNA polymerase, which explains its use in RNA virus infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ribavirin mimics purine structure and is incorporated into the growing nucleic acid strand, halting elongation. As a guanine analog it is effective against viral RNA polymerase, which makes it useful against RNA viruses such as RSV and hepatitis C virus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The M2 ion channel is the target of amantadine and rimantadine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Protease inhibition is not the described mechanism of ribavirin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: DNA polymerase is the target of guanosine analogs such as acyclovir and ganciclovir.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neuraminidase is the target of oseltamivir and zanamivir in influenza.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man is receiving ribavirin with interferon alfa for hepatitis C. Routine laboratory monitoring is performed. Which of the following abnormalities is most likely?

explanation.summary: Ribavirin, particularly with concurrent interferon, causes neutropenia along with anemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ribavirin is associated with anemia, hemolytic anemia, and neutropenia, and headache, neutropenia, anemia, and myalgia are all reported with concurrent use of interferon. Blood counts therefore need monitoring during hepatitis C therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Eosinophilia is not a described laboratory effect of ribavirin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hypercalcemia is not among the reported adverse effects of this drug.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ribavirin causes anemia through hemolysis rather than raising the red cell mass.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An elevated platelet count is not an expected effect of ribavirin therapy.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A lung transplant recipient with severe RSV pneumonia is started on ribavirin. This drug belongs to which of the following classes?

explanation.summary: Ribavirin is classified as a guanosine nucleotide analog with broad-spectrum antiviral activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ribavirin is a guanosine nucleotide analog and broad-spectrum nucleoside antiviral. It inhibits nucleic acid synthesis in RNA viruses and is the only drug used for RSV, reserved for severely immunocompromised patients such as transplant recipients.

whyWrongByChoice.B: M2 ion channel blockers are amantadine and rimantadine, no longer used for influenza.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neuraminidase inhibitors are oseltamivir and zanamivir, used for influenza.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Blocking receptor attachment is not the described class or mechanism of ribavirin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ribavirin does not act by inhibiting a viral protease.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman took her first dose of oseltamivir yesterday for influenza. At today's visit she asks about receiving the live attenuated intranasal influenza vaccine. Which of the following is the most appropriate advice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cancel her vaccination permanently because of antiviral exposure

choices.label: B
choices.text: Defer the vaccine until at least 48 hours after the antiviral course

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give the vaccine now, since the interval applies only beforehand

choices.label: D
choices.text: Give the vaccine only if she is also taking warfarin therapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Give the vaccine today, at the same time as the antiviral dose

explanation.summary: Live influenza vaccine is deferred until 48 hours after antiviral agents, because antivirals blunt the vaccine's effect.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antiviral agents may diminish the therapeutic effect of the influenza virus vaccine. Live influenza virus vaccine is avoided within 2 weeks before or 48 hours after administration of antiviral agents, so vaccination should wait until she has finished and cleared the drug.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The restriction is a timing issue, not a permanent contraindication.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The avoidance interval applies on both sides of antiviral administration.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Warfarin interacts with ribavirin and has nothing to do with vaccine timing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Simultaneous administration risks blunting the vaccine response.

questions.topicName: Antivirals 2 of 2: Drugs to Treat Influenza Virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection

questions.stem: A healthy 40-year-old man with influenza asks what an antiviral will realistically do for him. Which of the following best describes the expected benefit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Everyone in his household will be protected from illness

choices.label: B
choices.text: He may feel better about one day sooner than without it

choices.label: C
choices.text: His fever will break within one hour of the first dose

choices.label: D
choices.text: His symptoms will resolve about one week sooner than usual

choices.label: E
choices.text: The illness will be aborted completely within 12 hours

explanation.summary: In an otherwise healthy patient, the realistic benefit of a flu antiviral is feeling better roughly a day sooner.
explanation.whyCorrect: The benefit of influenza antivirals is not as obvious as with antibiotics for a bacterial infection. The most a patient can expect to gain is feeling better a day sooner than without the medicine, and the drugs work best when started early, before the window of opportunity has passed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Treating his illness does not guarantee protection for household contacts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: These drugs slow viral spread over days; they do not break fever within an hour.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A week of shortening greatly overstates the modest benefit of these agents.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antivirals do not abort influenza; the illness still runs a shortened course.
